text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ALL NEWSPAPERS

- OSCE Commissioner for national minorities, Max van der Stoel, arrived on one-day visit to Latvia. He called on natuaralisation tests to be made easier for those applying for Latvian citizenship, who are mainly ethnic Russian-speakers.

- President Guntis Ulmanis suggested that the terms of enforcing the pension law should be revised. The mechanism of calculating pensions should be changed to level out a sharp difference of pensions between those who retired last year and this year.
- Adolfs Sadauskis, well-known businessman and president of the company Domeniks, the Mercedes-Benz distributor in Latvia, died in a car crash.

- The leaders of leading parties Latvia's Way and Fatherland & Freedom discussed the situation over the dispute in the Latvian Privatisation Agency. They agreed economic issues should not be politicised to avoid destabilisation of the cabinet.
- Consumer prices in Latvia were up 0.4 percent in March.
DIENA
- Latvia's Way parliament faction leader Andrejs Pantelejevs said the government should carry out an objective poll to see why so many non-citizens are reluctant to be naturalised.
- The foreign ministry views positively the proposal of the Danish government to form a co-ordination group for security issues in the Baltics.
- Popular Latvian composer Raimonds Pauls, whose official post is cultural advisor to president Ulmanis, said in an interview to Diena that he may be a candidate in the next parliament elections.
NEATKARIGA RITA AVIZE
- The government approved spending 32 million lats from the privatisation fund.
- A meeting between delegations of Latvia and Lithuania on the maritime border is due to take place in Vilnius on April 10.
- On April 7-9 Jurmala will host the 4th Baltic congress on acupuncture and non-traditional medicine.
- The head of Riga customs, Vigo Leitholds, believes himself to have become a victim of a blackmail campaign.
BIZNES & BALTIYA
- The cabinet commitee approved an increase in the number of shares Latvia owns in the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development to 1,000. The shares are worth 10 million Ecu.
- A two-day regional conference of industrialists and entrepreneurs opened in Jurmala on April 7.
- Crude oil exports through Ventspils are booming. The oil export quota via pipelines for the second quarter of 1997 is set at 3.457 million tonnes, 110,000 tonnes more than in the first quarter.
SM
- Russia has extradited to Latvia four criminals involved in holding up an accountant's car in 1993.
DIENAS BIZNESS
- 21 Latvian companies will participate in the Hannover industrial technology fair on April 14-19.
- Unibanka shares fell strongly on Monday.
